newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T. declines comment on demerger report.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T. declines comment on demerger report.

text.p: British finance and tobacco group B.A.T. Industries Plc on Wednesday declined to comment on fresh reports that it was preparing to announce a full demerger of its main business interests.
A spokesman said the company never commented on market rumours.

However, he said, the group's position had not changed since the AGM at the end of April, when chairman Lord Cairns said the company had an open mind on its future structure and there were "no sacred cows".

A report in Wednesday's Guardian Newspaper said documents circulating in London's financial district suggested that B.A.T. had decided its financial arm, which includes Eagle Star and Allied Dunbar, was strong enough to stand alone.
It said B.A.T. would announce full demerger plans shortly, with a spin-off completed by the end of the year.
Shares in B.A.T. climbed sharply in early trading, trading at 560 1/2 pence midmorning. However, they were below an early peak of 565 pence.
Analysts believe a demerger makes more sense for B.A.T. now that a settlement has been reached over tobacco litigation, which affected the value of its American subsidiary Brown & Williamson.
